  play:
    name: 'Leg: Play (Android external beta)'
    # Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic (unchanged by #359 — only the leg's START moved):
    # child wc 95m (version 20 + build-android 45 + submit-android 30);
    # 240m leg > worst-case + ~15m margin. Waits are read-only (gh-1903) —
    # no cancel, no re-dispatch, bounded by the child's per-job timeouts
    # (#344) and this leg timeout.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'play')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # Secrets presence is checked in the first step — while the Play
      # upload keystore/service account are not configured, the leg green-
      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).
      PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
      ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
      ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'play'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=play) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Skip without Play secrets (green-neutral)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          missing=""
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD"
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            missing="$missing PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON"
          fi
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play secrets not configured (missing:${missing}) — the Android leg skips green-neutrally until the upload keystore + Play service account secrets exist (issue #289 owner checklist)."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "All Play secrets present — dispatching the Android build+upload."

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # all: build + Play upload + LISTING deploy (issue #947) — the
          # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device
          # type and verifies it via edits.images.list, so the listing can
          # never trail the committed goldens by more than one train.
          # beta = the external/open testing track, mirroring the iOS leg's
          # external TestFlight group (#239 pattern).
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # Since #359 the TestFlight
          # sibling leg fires CONCURRENTLY with this one (both needs: plan)
          # and dispatches the SAME workflow in the same minute —
          # correlation is by the child's run-name ("build-mobile
          # (all/none)" vs the sibling's "(none/all)", pinned by
          # test), never by "first run in the window", with newest-match +
          # the 30s window. Read-only wait (gh-1903): a wedged/queued run
          # is NEVER cancelled or re-dispatched — build-android/submit-
          # android's own timeout-minutes (#344) and this leg's 240m are
          # the only bounds; on leg timeout only this leg's own
          # never-started orphan child is cancelled.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (all/none)' \
            -f android_content=all -f android_track=beta -f ios_content=none \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  cli:
    name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 335m (version 20 + build-macos 150×2 — the
    # arm64 AND x86_64 matrix legs SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
    # macOS runner — + release-macos 15); 360m leg ≥ worst-case + margin
    # (both build-macos jobs carry 150m server-side timeouts, #344). A
    # queued child — including one waiting out a sibling's full 150m
    # matrix leg — is NEVER cancelled (gh-1903); the leg timeout bounds
    # the wait and the watcher orphan-cancels only a never-started child.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'cli')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'cli'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=cli) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-macos.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Children derive version themselves (latest tag + 1 at their own
          # dispatch moment) — a tag pinned here would race auto_release and
          # could attach assets to a tag pointing at a different commit.
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343):
          # correlates OUR run by the child's run-name
          # ("build-macos (create_release=true)") so a concurrent human
          # dispatch is never adopted. A wedged self-hosted run is NEVER
          # cancelled/re-dispatched — the bounds are the build-macos jobs'
          # own 150m server-side timeouts (#344) and this leg's 360m; on
          # leg timeout the watcher orphan-cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started child.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-macos.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-macos (create_release=true)' \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  website:
    name: 'Leg: Website'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 60m (pages build 45 + deploy 15); 180m leg
    # ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could not
    # even fit a healthy child + appear window — the 180m leg is the
    # #351 sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'website')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'website'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=website) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # pages.yml is path-filtered on push, so routine pushes (e.g. lib/
      # changes outside its filters) never redeploy — the daily guarantees
      # fa1.dev tracks main.
      - name: Dispatch pages.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # pages.yml takes no inputs, so there is no displayTitle to
          # disambiguate on — the watcher falls back to
          # newest-in-tight-window and waits read-only: no cancel, no
          # re-dispatch, bounded by the pages jobs' own timeout-minutes
          # (#344) and this leg's 180m.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh pages.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  addin:
    name: 'Leg: Outlook add-in'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 45m (single office-addin-suite job); 150m
    # leg ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could
    # not even fit a healthy child + appear window — 150m is the #351
    # sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 150
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'addin')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'addin'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=addin) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # Acceptance suite (manifest validation, dart2js taskpane, Node +
      # Playwright e2e). The fa1.dev /outlook publish itself rides the
      # website leg — pages.yml assembles the same add-in into the deploy.
      - name: Dispatch office-addin.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # No inputs to disambiguate on (newest-in-tight-window
          # fallback); the wait is bounded by the office-addin-suite
          # job's own 45m timeout (#344) and this leg's 150m — never by a
          # watcher cancel.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh office-addin.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  # ── pub.dev leg ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
  # only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs — a schedule/dispatch run can never
  # satisfy it). This leg VERIFIES pub.dev serves the pubspec version and,
  # when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
  # gh-1192: a tag-publish still EXECUTING (tag pushed, ci run not visible
  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window) is
  # classified «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh —
  # a neutral skip (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled
  # daily re-verifies. The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml
  # run» error one minute before the healthy run completed (#1189, false
  # alarm). gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG (the
  # committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder), so the «tag not cut
  # yet» state no longer exists.

  pubdev:
    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'pubdev'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
          exit 1

      # gh-1561: the never-triggered self-heal re-pushes the latest tag with
      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped (job-level permissions block).
      # Shape mirrors the validator-proven precedent (ci.yml release job,
      # the create-github-app-token step): NO `if:` at all — secrets
      # context in a step-if trips GitHub's workflow validator; and a mint
      # on an unconfigured App (forks, rotation gap) fails, is SWALLOWED by
      # continue-on-error, outputs.token stays empty, and the script's
      # manual-re-push alarm fires exactly as before this change.
      # Least privilege, verified against the PINNED action (v3.2.0,
      # bcd2ba49 — review thread 10): the composite `permissions` input
      # does NOT exist there (action.yml defines only the generated
      # `permission-*` inputs — GitHub warns `Unexpected input(s)
      # 'permissions'` and the action never reads it; ci.yml:3980 rides
      # that warning). The HONORED ceiling is the granular
      # `permission-contents` input, which the action turns into the mint
      # request's permissions map: contents:write only — the tag re-push —
      # instead of the installation's full grant set. Without it the token
      # inherits every permission the fa-release-bot installation has.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        id: app-token
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permission-contents: write

      - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
        id: check
        # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
        # RELEASE_APP_TOKEN is empty when the mint above skipped (App not
        # configured) — the script then fails over to the manual-re-push
        # alarm instead of attempting a re-arm.
        env:
          RELEASE_APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh

  # ── Release-draft sweeper (issue #282) ────────────────────────────────────
  # Hygiene leg: no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind (the
  # 3-week-old v0.1.190 rot). The per-job guards in build-macos/build-mobile
  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that
  # slips through (a cancelled run, a path without a guard) is deleted after
  # 24h and a deduplicated self-closing issue names the creating run so a
  # RECURRING stuck draft points at its broken step instead of rotting.
  # Runs on every daily (and manual) invocation regardless of leg results —
  # change-gating must not gate hygiene.
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue
        run: bash scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh

  # ── Report + self-healing issues ─────────────────────────────────────────
  report:
    name: Summary + self-filed issues
    needs: [plan, testflight, play, pubdev, cli, website, addin]
    if: always() # runs even when plan failed, so plan failures enter the self-healing loop too
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Job summary table and issue lifecycle
        env:
          NEXT_TAG: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
          PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
          DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT: ${{ needs.testflight.result }}
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT_URL: ${{ needs.testflight.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PLAY: ${{ needs.play.result }}
          LEG_PLAY_URL: ${{ needs.play.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PUBDEV: ${{ needs.pubdev.result }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_STATUS: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.status }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBSPEC: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.pubspec_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.published_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_URL: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_CLI: ${{ needs.cli.result }}
          LEG_CLI_URL: ${{ needs.cli.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_WEBSITE: ${{ needs.website.result }}
          LEG_WEBSITE_URL: ${{ needs.website.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_ADDIN: ${{ needs.addin.result }}
          LEG_ADDIN_URL: ${{ needs.addin.outputs.run_url }}
        run: bash scripts/daily_publish_report.sh

      # gh-1478: the inject_failure TEST hook must prove the filed digest
      # QUOTES the injected ::error:: line (signal-first excerpt via the
      # per-job log endpoint), not merely that an issue exists — the #1473
      # tree-noise regression class.
      # The `!= ''` guard matters: on schedule triggers the `inputs` context
      # is EMPTY (the dispatch `default: none` does not apply), so gating
      # only on `!= 'none'` would run — and fail — this step every cron run.
      - name: Verify injected-failure excerpt (TEST)
        if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
        env:
          INJECTED: ${{ inputs.inject_failure }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          title="[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed"
          n=$(gh issue list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --state open \
                --label daily-publish --limit 200 \
                --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' \
                | while IFS=$'\t' read -r num t; do
                    [ "$t" = "$title" ] && echo "$num"
                  done | head -1)
          if [ -z "$n" ]; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: no open issue titled '${title}' — the self-filing path regressed"
            exit 1
          fi
          text=$(gh issue view "$n" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
                   --json body,comments --jq '.body, (.comments[]?.body // empty)')
          if ! grep -qF "injected failure (inject_failure=${INJECTED})" <<< "$text"; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: issue #${n} never quotes the injected ::error:: line — the signal-first excerpt regressed (gh-1478)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "inject_failure verify OK: issue #${n} quotes the injected error line (gh-1478)"

"""Per-artifact uncompressed size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1).

Emits the per-entry uncompressed size table (the issue's inventory format)
for a shipped artifact and fails the build when any tracked line regresses
beyond the budget (default +5%).

Usage:
  size_manifest.py emit   <artifact> [--min-bytes N]        # TSV to stdout
  size_manifest.py check  <artifact> --baseline FILE
                          [--budget-pct 5] [--init-if-missing]
                          [--manifest-out FILE] [--forbid REGEX]...
                          [--vendored REGEX]... [--strict-vendored]
  size_manifest.py selftest

`<artifact>` is a zip-family file (.zip/.ipa/.aab — uncompressed entry sizes
via zipfile) or a directory (tree of file sizes, for the web deploy root).

Manifest format (TSV; every row is `<bytes>\t<name>`, path-sorted. TOTAL
is an ordinary row — `<total_bytes>\tTOTAL` — and sorts among the paths;
do not rely on its position, the parser keys by name):
  <uncompressed_bytes>\t<path>
  <total_bytes>\tTOTAL

a content/rev-hash directory — the Flutter engine renderer artifacts
(canvaskit/skwasm) move under a new one on every 3.47.x patch drop while
the byte sizes stay identical. Both the artifact scan and the baseline
load collapse such segments to `<rev>` BEFORE diffing, so an engine rev
bump lands as an in-place UPDATE (the usual size-band compare) instead
of N brand-new heavyweight lines. Normalization is idempotent, so
pre-fix baselines carrying the literal rev hash migrate on load — no
baseline rewrite needed. Colliding normalized rows (two rev dirs in one
artifact, e.g. stale files) merge to the heavier one.

Gate semantics (`check`):
  - growth > budget%% on any baseline line or on the first-party TOTAL
    -> FAIL
  - NEW line heavier than 5%% of the baseline first-party TOTAL -> FAIL
    (catches re-adding removed weight, e.g. a dropped interpreter coming
    back — re-growth must be a conscious ack)

    REGEX) are engine payload, not our growth — their breaches print
    ::warning and stay out of the failure count, and they are excluded
    from the TOTAL the budget compares (first-party TOTAL = TOTAL minus

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Package browser_ext/ into build/fa-extension.zip (runtime files only:
# manifest, sw/, content/, panel/ — README, dart/ sources, test/, and
# compiled artifacts' side files stay out).
# `--with-app` first builds the Flutter web app (flutter_app/ → build/web) and
# bundles it as browser_ext/app/ so the side panel hosts the full fa app.
# browser_ext/app/ is a build artifact (gitignored, never committed).
# Compiles the embedded Dart agent first when a Dart SDK is available
# (scripts must FAIL LOUDLY on compile errors — CI always builds it).
# Without dart: a previously built sw/agent.js ships if present, else the
# zip is scaffold-only with a warning (never a failure).
# Runs green on ubuntu-latest and macOS: needs zip + python3|node|grep.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

with_app=0
case "${1:-}" in
  --with-app) with_app=1 ;;
  "") ;;
  *) echo "unknown option: $1 (usage: $0 [--with-app])" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

manifest=browser_ext/manifest.json

# The manifest carries // comments (Chrome's parser is lenient, strict
# JSON validators are not) — strip them before validating, the same
# regex test/browser_ext/chrome_driver.dart uses.
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -c '
import json, re, sys
raw = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
json.loads(re.sub(r"^\s*//.*$", "", raw, flags=re.M))
' "$manifest"
elif command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  node -e 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, ""))' "$manifest"
else
  grep -q '"manifest_version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*3' "$manifest"
fi

# --- Vendored engine assets (gh-1630 I2): fetched ONLY from
# browser_ext/vendor.lock.json, SHA-256-verified, fail-loud on mismatch.
# Covers the offscreen run_script runtimes AND the panel app's on-device
# engines (pyodide/quickjs/sql.js/webllm/transformers/litert). ---
"$(dirname "$0")/fetch_vendor_assets.sh"

# --- Embedded agent (dart2js). Output is a build artifact: never committed. ---
agent_js=browser_ext/sw/agent.js
if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "building embedded agent (dart2js)…"
  ( cd browser_ext/dart \
    && dart pub get >/dev/null \
    && dart compile js -O2 -o ../sw/agent.js agent_main.dart )
  rm -f "${agent_js}.deps" "${agent_js}.map"
elif [ -f "$agent_js" ]; then
  echo "dart SDK not found — shipping prebuilt $agent_js"
else
  echo "WARNING: no dart SDK and no prebuilt sw/agent.js — scaffold-only zip (embedded agent disabled)"
fi

# --- Optional fa web app (flutter_app → browser_ext/app). Build artifact. ---
if [ "$with_app" -eq 1 ]; then
  if ! command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: --with-app passed but flutter is not installed — cannot build browser_ext/app/" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "building fa web app (flutter build web --release)…"
  # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile — in the
  # build-macos release job this script's pub get is the ONLY
  # flutter_app resolution, so a plain resolve would float a
  # pubspec/lockfile skew into a green release build.
  # --base-href MUST match the panel-relative location: panel.js resolves
  # 'app/index.html' against panel/panel.html, so the bundle lives at
  # browser_ext/panel/app/ (a root-level copy is invisible to the panel).
  ( cd flutter_app && flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile >/dev/null
    # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (pubspec.yaml),
    # so the web build dies bundling it when the file is absent (#140).
    # Create it AFTER pub get — pub get removes a placeholder touched
    # earlier (runs 34593431895, 34596707238) — and keep it non-empty:
    # the populated placeholder is the shape build-macos.yml's app job
    # has shipped green. A real local .env (developer keys) is never

[ $# -ge 1 ] || usage
CMD="$1"; shift

kc_password() {
  # Keychain password: [REDACTED:Sensitive-Value] if provided, else a stored
  # random one (created on first use). 0600 user-only file — it protects a
  # CI-only keychain whose certificates are already provisioned from repo
  # secrets by a trusted workflow.
  if [ -n "${CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ ! -s "$KCPASS_FILE" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$CFG"
    umask 077
    openssl rand -base64 32 > "$KCPASS_FILE"
  fi
  cat "$KCPASS_FILE"
}

ensure_keychain() {
  local kcpass
  kcpass="$(kc_password)"
  if [ ! -f "$KC" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$CFG"
    security create-keychain -p "$kcpass" "$KC"
  fi
  # gh-1954: NEVER auto-lock (-t 0, no -l). The retired "-l -t 86400"
  # (lock on sleep + 24h backstop) assumed "every ci-sign entry point
  # unlocks anyway" — but gym's `xcodebuild -showBuildSettings` is NOT a
  # ci-sign entry point: it runs ~15 min after the unlock and hit a locked
  # keychain's GUI password prompt on the headless runner (4 retries,
  # fastlane timeout, run 40849468765). Settings only apply
  # non-interactively on a FRESH keychain; on an existing one the command
  # prompts (GUI session) or fails silently (headless, masked by || true).
  # gh-2008 FINAL: set-keychain-settings is DELETED. Proven on this host
  # (macOS 26, GUI session): the call raises the SecurityAgent password
  # dialog EVEN AFTER a successful unlock-keychain -p (wave 05:23:45Z,
  # alarm 14 kill — the orphan dialog the owner kept seeing). It never
  # applied non-interactively on an existing keychain anyway (see the
  # gh-1963 notes) and never provided anti-lock: that job belongs to the
  # point-of-use unlocks + the Fastfile unlock watchdog (gh-1965).
  security unlock-keychain -p "$kcpass" "$KC"
  # Idempotent, additive, self-verifying search-list membership (gh-1866
  # logic, applied ONCE for a persistent entry — never per job). Skipped
  # for test keychains (CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN override) — they never leave the
  # test sandbox.
  # gh-1972: rewrite the search list DEFENSIVELY — the naive append once
  # produced a garbled list (System duplicated, login.keychain-db missing,
  # default dangling → "A keychain cannot be found to store" GUI dialogs
  # and gh auth failures on the shared host). Dedupe, keep login FIRST,
  # append ci-signing LAST, always write the full explicit list.
  if [ -z "${CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN:-}" ]; then
    local rest login_kc
    login_kc="$HOME/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db"
    rest="$(security list-keychains | sed 's/[[:space:]]//g; s/"//g' | grep -v '^$' | grep -vxF "$KC" | grep -vxF "$login_kc" | awk '!seen[$0]++')"
    if [ -f "$login_kc" ]; then
      security list-keychains -d user -s "$login_kc" $rest "$KC"
    else
      security list-keychains -d user -s $rest "$KC"
    fi
    security list-keychains | sed 's/[[:space:]]//g; s/"//g' | grep -qxF "$KC" || die "failed to add keychain to search list"
  fi
}

do_unlock() {
  [ -f "$KC" ] || die "no signing keychain at $KC — run 'ci-sign install <label>' first (host provisioning)"
  security unlock-keychain -p "$(kc_password)" "$KC"
}

p12_env_value() { # p12_env_value <VARNAME>
  local var="$1"
  [ -n "${!var:-}" ] || die "env $var is not set"
  printf '%s' "${!var}"
}

1. Stale ~/bin/ci-sign (pre-gh-2008) on the self-hosted runner still calls `set-keychain-settings -t 0` inside ensure_keychain on EVERY install/unlock invocation.
2. That call raises the SecurityAgent GUI dialog EVERY time (proven per gh-2008), alarm-killed after 5s but leaving ORPHAN SecurityAgent dialogs on the host GUI.
3. Those orphan dialogs / GUI state then hang the NEXT `security import` (x86_64, 2h27m → "User canceled") — the exact class gh-1954/gh-2008 document.
4. And the identity resolution flakiness in arm64's xcodebuild ("No certificate...") matches the keychain GUI-prompt wedging class.

The REPO FIX for the signing lane: run the `install` step in the build-macos (matrix) job before any ci-sign call — the comment already DECLARES this intent ("re-install it to the host PATH on every signing job so ~/bin/ci-sign can never drift") but the step was wired into the ubuntu version job instead. That's a genuine bug: the authoritative-copy invariant is not enforced on the machines that execute ci-sign.

Let me verify by checking git history: when was the install added and where?

JOB   version: ->     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
JOB   build-macos: ->     runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
   CALL in   build-macos: :             ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos
   CALL in   build-macos: :             CERT_SHA1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 fa-macos)
   CALL in   build-macos: :             # goes through ci-sign plist — the legacy CMS decoder needs a
   CALL in   build-macos: :             PROFILE_UUID=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract UUID raw -)
   CALL in   build-macos: :             PROFILE_NAME=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Name raw -)
   CALL in   build-macos: :             PROFILE_TEAM=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract TeamIdentifier.0 raw - 2>/dev/null || true)
   CALL in   build-macos: :               ~/bin/ci-sign doctor profile.provisionprofile fa-macos
   CALL in   build-macos: :             ~/bin/ci-sign unlock
   CALL in   build-macos: :             nohup bash -c 'while :; do sleep 60; ~/bin/ci-sign unlock >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done' \
   CALL in   build-macos: :             echo "ci-sign unlock watchdog armed (pid $(cat ci-sign-watchdog.pid), 60s cadence — gh-1986)"
   CALL in   build-macos: :               # gh-1865 model v3: profile decoding via ci-sign plist —
   CALL in   build-macos: :               APP_ID=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Entitlements xml1 -o - - | grep -A 1 'com.apple.application-identifier' | tail -1 | sed 's/.*<string>\(.*\)<\/string>.*/\1/')
   CALL in   build-macos: :               ~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile > profile_decoded.plist
   CALL in   build-macos: :           ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos-installer
   CALL in   build-macos: :           INSTALLER_SHA1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 fa-macos-installer)
   CALL in   build-macos: :             if ps -p "$WPID" -o command= 2>/dev/null | grep -q "ci-sign unlock"; then
   CALL in   build-macos: :               echo "ci-sign unlock watchdog stopped (pid $WPID)"
   CALL in   build-macos: :               echo "ci-sign unlock watchdog pid $WPID no longer running — nothing to stop"
JOB   build-macos-cli: ->     runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
JOB   build-extension: ->     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
JOB   release-macos: ->     runs-on: ubuntu-latest

log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = job-name fragment
  # gh-1478: signal-first excerpt. Grep the failed log for error signal
  # lines and quote the first matches with context; the raw tail is only
  # the fallback when nothing matches (the #1473 tree-noise digest).
  local raw=""
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    raw=$(gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | tail -n 400 || true)
  fi
  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
    # No child log (child in flight/cancelled, or never dispatched). The
    # RUN-level log zip is 409 while the daily run is in progress, but the
    # per-JOB log endpoint serves completed jobs — resolve the failed or
    # cancelled leg job and take ITS log (the #1472 empty-shrug class, and
    # the inject_failure TEST hook shape: a failed leg job, no child run).
    local job_id
    job_id=$(gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg frag "$2" '
        [.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                          and (.name | contains($frag))) | .databaseId]
        | last // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$job_id" ]; then
      raw=$(gh run view --job "$job_id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -n 400 || true)
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$raw" | signal_excerpt
}

signal_excerpt() { # stdin: log text; stdout: first signal matches w/ context, else tail
  awk '
    { lines[NR] = $0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::|Message from server|(^|[^A-Za-z])error:|(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL|[Ee]xit code|exited with/) {
        if (++hits <= 3)
          for (i = NR - 3; i <= NR + 3; i++) if (i >= 1) want[i] = 1
      }
    }
    END {
      if (hits == 0) { # no signal line — the raw tail is the fallback
        start = NR - 49; if (start < 1) start = 1
        for (i = start; i <= NR; i++) print lines[i]
        exit
      }
      i = 1; snip = 0
      while (i <= NR) {
        if (!want[i]) { i++; continue }
        if (snip++) print "[...]"
        while (i <= NR && want[i]) { print lines[i]; i++ }
      }
    }'
}

trap 'rm -f "$rows"' EXIT

gh label create daily-publish --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── log collection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Failing job/step names and the last ~50 log lines, from the child run when
# one exists, else from this daily run's leg job (jobs API — the run is
# still in progress here, and GitHub serves no logs for it mid-run).
failing_steps() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = log prefix
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --json jobs --jq '
      [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
        | .name + " — " +
          ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
            | .name] | join(", "))]
      | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  else
    # The report job runs INSIDE the daily run, so the run is still in
    # progress here — and GitHub serves no logs for in-progress runs
    # (--log-failed returns empty: issue #208 was filed as "unknown (job
    # cancelled or timed out)" for a leg that died in 4s with a clear
    # error). Job/step data IS served mid-run — read failed steps from it.
    gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
      | jq -r --arg job "$2" '
          [.jobs[] | select(.name == $job
                              and (.conclusion == "failure"
                                or .conclusion == "cancelled"))
            | .name + " — " +
              ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure"
                               or .conclusion == "cancelled")

file_or_comment() { # $1 = leg id, $2 = log prefix, $3 = child run url, $4 = leg result
  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  # Job-name fragment for the own-run jobs API (the yaml display names add
  # parentheticals the report's display names don't carry).
  local frag="${prefix%% (*}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body sig
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$frag")
  sig=""
  [ -z "$excerpt" ] || sig=$(printf '%s\n' "$excerpt" | error_signature)

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."
      # gh-1478: a cancelled run gets a real digest — which job was in
      # flight, its timeout-minutes ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of
      # the #1472 empty "no failed-step log available" shrug.
      local cinfo cname cstart cend ceiling
      cinfo=$(cancelled_job_info "$frag")
      ceiling=$(leg_ceiling_minutes "$frag")
      if [ -n "$cinfo" ]; then
        IFS=$'\t' read -r cname cstart cend <<< "$cinfo"
        local celapsed="unknown"
        local cs="" ce=""
        cs=$(iso_to_epoch "$cstart" || true)
        ce=$(iso_to_epoch "$cend" || true)
        if [ -n "$cs" ] && [ -n "$ce" ] && [ "$ce" -ge "$cs" ]; then
          celapsed=$(fmt_elapsed $((ce - cs)))
        fi
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** job \`$cname\` — killed after ${celapsed} elapsed."
        if [ -n "$ceiling" ]; then
          echo "**Timeout ceiling:** \`${ceiling}m\` (timeout-minutes in daily-publish.yml)."
          if [ "$celapsed" != "unknown" ]; then
            local csec_elapsed=$((ce - cs)) csec_ceiling=$((ceiling * 60))
            if [ "$csec_elapsed" -ge $((csec_ceiling - 60)) ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — at the ceiling, so the leg hit its own timeout (a wedged child or too-tight ceiling; the child chain timeouts are the #351 arithmetic)."
            elif [ "$((csec_elapsed * 2))" -le "$csec_ceiling" ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — far below the ceiling, so this looks like a whole-run/operator cancellation or an infrastructure kill, not the leg's own timeout."
            else
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — below the ceiling; check the run timeline for a whole-run cancellation before treating this as a leg defect."
            fi
          fi
        fi
      else
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** could not resolve which job was in flight from the jobs API — see the run timeline."
      fi
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
      # The normalized signature is both human-visible and machine-matchable
      # (root-cause dedup searches open issues' bodies/comments for it).
      echo "**Error signature:** \`$sig\`"
      echo "<!-- daily-publish-sig: $sig -->"
    fi
    echo
    echo "Failure excerpt (signal-first: error lines with context; raw tail when no signal line matches):"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: when the normalized signature matches an OPEN
  # issue's body/comments (any label — #1452 is not a daily-publish issue),

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '

}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  # The fragment is matched LITERALLY (index, not ~): it contains the CLI
  # leg's `+` ("Leg: CLI + macOS desktop"), which as an unescaped awk ERE
  # operator never matches the workflow yaml — that silently dropped the
  # CLI leg's timeout ceiling from cancelled digests.
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    index($0, "name: ") > 0 && index($0, frag) > 0 { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      # verified outcome (up-to-date/recovered/private) closes it.
      if [[ "$override" == "skipped:"* ]]; then
        icon="⏭️"
        status="$override"
      else
        icon="✅"
        status="${override:-success}"
        close_if_open "$id"
      fi
      ;;
    failure)
      icon="❌"; status="failure"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url"
      ;;
    cancelled)
      icon="⚠️"; status="cancelled (timeout?)"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url" "cancelled"
      ;;
    *)
      icon="⏭️"; status="skipped"
      ;;

341:process_leg() {
process_leg() {
  local id="$1" display="$2" result="${3:-}" url="${4:-}" version="${5:-}" links="${6:-}" override="${7:-}"
  local prefix="Leg: $2" icon status
  case "$result" in
    success)
      # A neutral-skip override («skipped: …») marks an UNOBSERVED outcome
      # (#1368 false green: release-in-flight rendered ✅ and auto-closed the
      # leg's stuck-release issue without ever seeing the publish). Render it
      # as a skip — never ✅ — and keep any open leg issue open; only a
      # verified outcome (up-to-date/recovered/private) closes it.
      if [[ "$override" == "skipped:"* ]]; then
        icon="⏭️"
        status="$override"
      else
        icon="✅"
        status="${override:-success}"
        close_if_open "$id"
      fi
      ;;
    failure)
      icon="❌"; status="failure"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url"
      ;;
    cancelled)
      icon="⚠️"; status="cancelled (timeout?)"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url" "cancelled"

- name: Provision signing via ci-sign (persistent host keychain)
        id: ios_signing
        env:
          IOS_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_BASE64 }}
          IOS_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: IOS_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: IOS_P12_PASSWORD
          IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
          IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1865: the repo copy of ci-sign is authoritative —
          # re-install it to the host PATH on every signing job so
          # ~/bin/ci-sign can never drift from the reviewed source.
          # gh-1954: install(1) does not create parent directories —
          # on a fresh runner $HOME/bin does not exist (run 40822964468,
          # "install: invalid target .../bin/ci-sign: No such file").
          mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"
          install -m 755 scripts/ci-sign "$HOME/bin/ci-sign"
          # gh-1865 model v3 (owner decision 2026-10-28): NO per-job
          # keychains and NO user-global keychain writes. ~/bin/ci-sign

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate

# to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2030 `[daily-publish] cli leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The daily-publish `cli` leg (daily run 41276389088) failed because its child `build-macos.yml` run 41276487426 (dispatched with `create_release=true`) concluded `failure` — three of its jobs failed, so `Create macOS GitHub Release` skipped and the leg went red.

**Root cause** (two independent, repo-owned causes; one infra aggravator):

1. **Deterministic — stale size floor (RC1).** The `Build Chrome extension` job failed at the size-budget gate: `GREW +7.9% sw/agent.js 1890859 -> 2040013` (budget +5%). `sw/agent.js` is `dart compile js -O2` of `browser_ext/dart/agent_main.dart`; the floor `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv` was last seeded 2026-10-19 (326eadd7). The last green gate (run 40637547009, 10-28) measured 1,941,731 (+2.7%); by 11-01 the compiled agent grew to 2,040,013 (+7.9%) — accumulated dart2js growth of ~12 days of legitimate main-Dart feature work feeding the embedded-agent import graph (scoped DAP channels #1888 + review hardening #1895, display-only redaction #1960, cross-module dedup #2023, media capabilities v2 #2007, control-flow quality #2021; bundle input grew 27,024,912 → 27,760,486 bytes). The gate did its ratchet job and correctly refused the growth; without a reseed the leg could NEVER go green (reproduced identically on the auto-rerun attempt 2 at 08:05Z). Fix: the gate's own documented remediation — `--reseed` from the failing run's artifact manifest (the gh-1820 arm64 and gh-1954 fa-ios precedents).

2. **Workflow wiring bug — stale `ci-sign` on the signing hosts (RC2).** Both macOS matrix jobs failed on signing. The `build-macos` job executes `~/bin/ci-sign` (install/sha1/plist/doctor/unlock + the installer identity) but never installs the repo-authoritative copy `scripts/ci-sign` — that step was wired ONLY into the `version` job, which runs on `ubuntu-latest` and never executes ci-sign (regression from gh-1865 model v3, ff49999d, 10-29 — the same day the signing lane first went red). The fa-m5 pool is one Mac with three runner registrations sharing `$HOME` (gh-2013), so every signing job executed whatever `host-signing-provision.yml` last copied. Provably stale: the run log shows `ci-sign: line 92: … Alarm clock: 14 … security set-keychain-settings -t 0` — a call that no main-branch revision has at line 92 (closest: c1464bb5/ccd7d3db line 111, f337168d line 115) and that gh-2008 FINAL (1978de3, 10-31) deleted entirely, because it raises the SecurityAgent GUI password dialog on every invocation and the 5s alarm kill leaves an ORPHAN dialog on the host screen. Consequences in this run: the x86_64 provisioning wedged 2h27m inside `security import` on the GUI prompt and died with `SecKeychainItemImport: User canceled the operation`; the arm64 xcodebuild died at 05:30:50 with `No certificate for team 'YP9HC3USZ3' matching '43AEC254…' found` (identity resolution destabilized by the same host GUI state class; gh-1954/gh-1972/gh-2008 document this family). Fix: install the authoritative repo copy at the top of the `build-macos` provisioning step — the exact shape `build-mobile.yml`'s iOS signing step has always used on the same runner pool. Host GUI state (orphan dialogs) may additionally need owner cleanup once; the fresh install stops the repo from recreating it.

**Impact**: The daily desktop/CLI release train (macOS DMG + CLI bundles + fa-extension.zip attached to the next tag) has not shipped since 10-27; the auto-filed issue carries no diagnostic signal (see note below).

**Fix approach**: (1) reseed `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv` from run 41276487426's gate-printed manifest via the real `size_manifest.py check --reseed` (the committed file is pinned byte-identical to the script's own output); (2) wire the authoritative ci-sign install into `build-macos.yml` before any ci-sign call.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first failure of this leg signature; not a returned ticket.

**Note (out of scope, observed)**: The issue body says "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" / "no failed-step log available" because `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh` reads the child run via `gh run view --json jobs` / `--log-failed`, which surface the LATEST attempt only — the child was re-run (attempt 2 started ~09:00:54Z) seconds before the report job's reads, hiding attempt 1's three failed jobs. The watcher (`dispatch_and_watch.sh`) itself behaved correctly (read-only wait, no cancel, correct failure verdict with child URL).

## Reproduction (TDD RED)

- `test/ci_2030_extension_size_floor_test.dart` — runs the REAL `size_manifest.py check` against the REAL committed floor with a directory fixture of run 41276487426's exact artifact shape (41 rows ≥ 64 KiB from the gate-printed manifest + sub-floor filler to the exact TOTAL 155,887,040). Before the fix it exits 1 with the exact leg failure: `GREW +7.9% sw/agent.js 1890859 -> 2040013`.
- `test/ci_2030_ci_sign_authoritative_copy_test.dart` — static workflow-shape assert: no `build-macos` step installed the repo copy of `scripts/ci-sign` before its first ci-sign call.

## Fix (GREEN)

- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv` — reseeded via `python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check <fixture> --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv --reseed`; deltas: `sw/agent.js` 1,890,859 → 2,040,013; `panel/app/main.dart.js` 12,117,285 → 12,343,041 (+1.9%, within budget); `panel/app/assets/NOTICES` −15,316 (shrank); TOTAL 155,539,998 → 155,887,040.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` — the `Provision signing via ci-sign` step now starts with `mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"` + `install -m 755 scripts/ci-sign "$HOME/bin/ci-sign"` (gh-1954 mkdir pairing preserved; the ubuntu `version` job's copy is left untouched — harmless there).
- Both tests above now pass; the size-floor test additionally pins the committed baseline as the byte-exact `--reseed` output for the shipped shape (no hand-edit drift).

arguments.newText:
2. **Workflow wiring bug — stale `ci-sign` on the signing hosts (RC2).** Both macOS matrix jobs failed on signing. The `build-macos` job executes `~/bin/ci-sign` (install/sha1/plist/doctor/unlock + the installer identity) but never installs the repo-authoritative copy `scripts/ci-sign` — that step was wired ONLY into the `version` job, which runs on `ubuntu-latest` and never executes ci-sign (regression from gh-1865 model v3, ff49999d, 10-29 — the same day the signing lane first went red). The fa-m5 pool is one Mac with three runner registrations sharing `$HOME` (gh-2013), so every signing job executed whatever `host-signing-provision.yml` last copied. Provably stale: the run log shows `ci-sign: line 92: … Alarm clock: 14 … security set-keychain-settings -t 0` — a call that no main-branch revision has at line 92 (closest: c1464bb5/ccd7d3db line 111, f337168d line 115) and that gh-2008 FINAL (1978de3, 10-31) deleted entirely, because it raises the SecurityAgent GUI password dialog on every invocation and the 5s alarm kill leaves an ORPHAN dialog on the host screen. Consequences in this run: the x86_64 provisioning wedged 2h27m inside `security import` on the GUI prompt and died with `SecKeychainItemImport: User canceled the operation`; the arm64 xcodebuild died at 05:30:50 with `No certificate for team 'YP9HC3USZ3' matching '43AEC254…' found` (identity resolution destabilized by the same host GUI state class; gh-1954/gh-1972/gh-2008 document this family). Fix: install the authoritative repo copy at the top of the `build-macos` provisioning step — the exact shape `build-mobile.yml`'s iOS signing step has always used on the same runner pool. Host GUI state (orphan dialogs) may additionally need owner cleanup once; the fresh install stops the repo from recreating it.

3. **Credential expiry — installer certificate (RC3, owner action required).** The auto-rerun (attempt 2, old tree) proved the host recovered once the GUI state cleared: `ci-sign: manifest matches but identity invalid — re-importing` completed in 0.5 s, the app identity installed green, and the FULL xcodebuild + app codesign succeeded (08:08–08:13). The job then died at the packaging step: `ci-sign: imported P12 for 'fa-macos-installer' but it is not a valid codesigning identity (expired, revoked, or key/cert mismatch)` — the **`MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64` Mac Installer Distribution certificate is expired or revoked**. That is a secret-rotation action in the Apple Developer Portal + repo secrets; no product-code change can fix it (ci-sign's fail-fast with the exact instruction is the designed behavior). Until rotated, the TestFlight-PKG lane keeps failing even with RC1/RC2 fixed (the DMG path is unaffected; the extension gate no longer blocks after RC1).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.

  (the #1364 lesson): one test red across N runs files ONE issue.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

- `Build Chrome extension` failed the size-budget ratchet: `GREW +7.9% sw/agent.js 1890859 -> 2040013` (budget +5%). The floor `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv` was seeded 2026-10-19; ~12 days of accumulated main-Dart feature work in the embedded-agent graph (DAP #1888/#1895, redaction #1960, dedup #2023, media #2007, quality #2021) grew the dart2js bundle past it. Deterministic — the auto-rerun failed the same gate.
- Both macOS archs failed signing because `build-macos` executes `~/bin/ci-sign` but never installs the repo-authoritative `scripts/ci-sign` — that step lived only in the ubuntu `version` job (gh-1865 regression). The host ran a stale pre-gh-2008 script whose `set-keychain-settings` raises orphan SecurityAgent dialogs (log: `Alarm clock: 14 … set-keychain-settings`), wedging the x86_64 `security import` for 2h27m (`User canceled the operation`) and destabilizing arm64's identity resolution.
- Residual (owner action, not repo-fixable): the auto-rerun proved the app identity + full build sign fine once the GUI state cleared — then failed at packaging with `imported P12 for 'fa-macos-installer' but it is not a valid codesigning identity (expired, revoked, or key/cert mismatch)`. The `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64` Mac Installer Distribution certificate must be re-issued and the secret rotated.

### Fix

- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded with the gate's own documented command (`size_manifest.py check --baseline … --reseed`) from run 41276487426's gate-printed manifest; `sw/agent.js` → 2,040,013, `main.dart.js` → 12,343,041 (+1.9%), NOTICES shrank, TOTAL → 155,887,040.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: the provisioning step now starts with `mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"` + `install -m 755 scripts/ci-sign "$HOME/bin/ci-sign"` — the exact shape `build-mobile.yml`'s iOS signing step uses on the same runner pool; reviewed gh-2008 changes can now actually reach the signing hosts.

### Root Cause

- The cli leg's `build-macos` run 41276487426 failed three jobs. `Build Chrome extension`: size-budget ratchet `GREW +7.9% sw/agent.js 1890859 -> 2040013` (budget +5%) — accumulated dart2js growth of the embedded-agent graph since the 2026-10-19 floor seed (DAP #1888/#1895, redaction #1960, dedup #2023, media #2007, quality #2021). ### Fix

- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded with the gate's own documented command (`size_manifest.py check --baseline … --reseed`) from the failing run's gate-printed manifest (sw/agent.js → 2,040,013, main.dart.js → 12,343,041, TOTAL → 155,887,040).
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: the provisioning step now installs the authoritative `scripts/ci-sign` first (`mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"` + `install -m 755 …`) — the shape `build-mobile.yml`'s iOS step always used.

### Test Coverage

- `test/ci_2030_extension_size_floor_test.dart` — RED first: the real gate + real committed floor against a fixture of the run's artifact shape exits 1 with the exact `GREW +7.9%` regression; GREEN after the reseed, plus a byte-exact `--reseed` round-trip pin (gh-1820 pattern).
- `test/ci_2030_ci_sign_authoritative_copy_test.dart` — workflow-shape guard: install must precede any ci-sign call in `build-macos` (RED before the fix).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: see ledger below.

### Notes

- Owner action required (not repo-fixable): the rerun proved the app identity + full build sign fine once host GUI state cleared, then failed packaging with `imported P12 for 'fa-macos-installer' but it is not a valid codesigning identity` — rotate the expired `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64`/`MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD` secrets; until then the TestFlight-PKG lane keeps failing (DMG + extension gate are unblocked).
